text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and searching for discount code handling.

The bug is clear: `_used_codes` is a module-level global set that records every code ever applied, so a reusable code is blocked after its first use. Let me check the tests to see what behavior is expected before changing it.
The tests confirm that discounts are reusable across separate orders. I'll remove the global "used" tracking so eligibility depends only on the subtotal threshold.

args.summary: Root cause: library/discounts.py kept a module-level set `_used_codes` and `apply_discount` added every applied code to it, while `is_eligible` rejected any code already in the set. So a reusable code like SAVE10 worked once per process and was then rejected for every later order until restart (matching the report). I removed the global set and the "used" check, so eligibility depends only on the subtotal vs. `min_subtotal`, as the existing tests (e.g. test_discount_object_is_reusable_across_separate_orders) expect. The full test suite passes (29/29).
